verdict_reason: 11 of the 12 tiles are the Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi or its immediate frontage, and the identification is by direct reading, not by the geotag. On 11922368215 the cocktail list's boxed footer reads 'Metropole's Century Specialty' above 'VND subject to 5% service charge and 10% VAT'; on 11923044274 the buffet card carries the hotel's interlocked-M monogram over 'Depuis 1901' and the chocolates are stamped with the same monogram. That exact monogram then reappears, moulded on the wall panels, in the second photographer's street frame 8564330323 - which independently ties that batch to the same hotel, so the two contributor blocks are not just co-pinned, they are co-located. 8570906229 shows the hotel's inner courtyard pool with its arched glazed pavilion, and the filigree cast-iron garden stair of 8565446760 stands against that same arched glazed gallery. The one photo that is not the hotel is 8565437674, and it is only ~60 m away: the Con Coc toad fountain in Dien Hong garden, directly across Ngo Quyen from the Metropole (a web check confirms the fountain's stone tower over eight carved dragons with water-spouting toads below, adjoining the Metropole and the State Bank). Remaining honest caveats: only two id blocks are present (11922/11923..., 8564-8570...), i.e. probably two photographers of the pile's stated four, and one tile is a photograph of a printed page rather than of a place.

photos.evidence: Cropped and upscaled 6x: a printed cocktail list ('LEGENDARY COCKTAILS', Daiquiri, Charlie Chaplin, Bloody Mary, Cosmopolitan, Mojito, Tom Collins, Margarita, Caipirinha, each with a Vietnamese sub-line) whose boxed footer reads 'Metropole's Century Specialty' beside the hotel monogram, over 'VND subject to 5% service charge and 10% VAT'.

A dark wood dessert/chocolate counter with glass shelves, small white place cards and a copper pan; same photographer and the same counter furniture as 11923044274, whose cards carry the Metropole monogram and 'Depuis 1901'.

Cropped and upscaled 5x: chocolate bonbons each stamped with an interlocked-M monogram in gold, and a white card printed with the same monogram above 'Depuis 1901' and the text 'Chocolate bonbon with coffee / So co la huong vi ca phe'. The monogram plus 1901 founding date is the Metropole's own mark.

An antique brass-and-wood candlestick telephone with a rotary dial standing on a dark marble top beside a white card - period lobby/bar prop, same photographer and same visit as the two frames whose printing names the Metropole.

A bartender in a white jacket pouring at a dark timber bar with backlit bottles and low lamps, two coupe glasses on the counter - the bar the 'Metropole's Century Specialty' cocktail list belongs to, same photographer-batch.

Upscaled 2.5x: a French-colonial facade seen through street trees - white render, moulded string courses, round-arched French windows with dark green louvred shutters and turned stone balustrades to each balcony. The shutter colour, balustrade pattern and render match the wing behind the hotel's cyclos in 8565420452, by the same photographer; kept at 0.6 because neighbouring colonial blocks (State Bank, Government Guest House) are similar in style.

Upscaled 2.5x, then 10x on the wall: wedding photographers crouching on a kerb shooting a bride and groom on a cobbled terrace in front of a white building with green awnings, wrought-iron canopy work, patio heaters and a chalkboard A-board. The rendered wall panels carry the same interlocked-M monogram read on the hotel's own buffet cards in 11923044274 - i.e. the Metropole's street-side terrace cafe.

This is a photograph of a printed page, not of a place: a hand-tinted archival elevated view of a French-colonial quarter (villas with slate and red-tiled roofs, a domed public building on the skyline, a formal garden and radiating avenues below) with a book caption running off the bottom edge, readable in part as '...to see what the French would have done to Singapore...'. The depicted scene is plausibly old Hanoi, but nothing identifies where the shutter was pressed.

Upscaled 2.5x: two vintage cyclos with olive canvas hoods parked on brick pavers beside a white colonial wing with dark green louvred shutters, clipped box topiary in black planters on the balcony above, and a doorman in dark uniform and peaked cap standing under the porte-cochere - the hotel's own cyclo fleet at its entrance; same photographer as the monogram-confirmed 8564330323.

Upscaled 2.5x, then 8x on the basin: a bride and groom sitting on the rim of a large circular stone fountain whose centre is a dark stone pier carrying a small colonnaded pavilion; carved dark stone dragons ring the base and, zoomed, a squat warty toad with drawn-up haunches sits below them spouting a jet of water. A web check of Dien Hong garden describes exactly this - a stone tower over eight carved stone dragons with water-spouting toads beneath, next to the Metropole and the State Bank - so this is the Con Coc (toad) fountain, about 60 m from the pin.

Upscaled 2.5x: a white filigree cast-iron staircase curving up from a lawn courtyard, beside a long gallery of tall arched glazed doors with green-painted frames, brick path, plumeria trees and green awnings beyond. The same arched glazed gallery, awnings and courtyard trees appear in 8570906229 by the same photographer, which is the hotel's pool courtyard.

Upscaled 2.2x, sepia-toned: a rectangular courtyard swimming pool after rain, wrought-iron tables and cross-back chairs on flagstones, sun-loungers and clipped shrubs in urns along the far side, an arched glazed conservatory pavilion with a trellis screen at right and the white multi-storey Heritage wing with tall shuttered windows and an awninged balustraded terrace behind - the Metropole's inner courtyard and Bamboo Bar pavilion.
